commits.title: A register puts every commerce table in a class, and a test holds it

changes.how: A pure module modelled on src/lib/personal-data.ts. Export `TABLE_CLASSES: Record<string, TableClass>` with one entry per base table of the commerce schema (486 today; list them with `rg -o '^CREATE TABLE commerce\.(\w+)' -r '$1' supabase/migrations/*_baseline_1_schema.sql | sort`, plus any table a later migration creates). `TableClass` is one of: `{ class: 'with_parent', parent: string }` (its rows go when the parent row goes: the table has a foreign key to `parent` with ON DELETE CASCADE, or the parent is the store), `{ class: 'deleted', kind: RetentionKind, step: string }` (deleted after the period of that kind in src/lib/retention.ts; `step` is 'file#function' of the code that holds the delete), `{ class: 'law', why: string }` (kept for bookkeeping or as the record: orders, invoices, credit notes, payments, the ledger, audit entries inside their period), `{ class: 'reference', why: string }` (reference or settings data that does not grow by time: countries, vat_rates, plans, retention_rules). This is the judgement part of the step: class each table by reading its migration and its pruner, not by its name. For a table already pruned by a constant elsewhere (the kinds in src/lib/retention.ts whose note says 'The code's constant is the source') use that kind. For a table pruned today with no kind (find them with `rg -n 'delete from commerce\.' src/server --glob '!*.test.*'`), add a kind for it in a second custom migration of this commit (same form as the previous commit's: widen retention_rules_kind, insert the seed row), or class it with_parent when its only growth is per parent. The seven tables of this step are 'deleted' with the kinds the previous commit added (cart_rows for carts, webhook_events, email_rows for email_messages, experiment_events, referral_visits, work_events, page_versions).

Uses createTestDatabase() as src/db/privacy.test.ts does. Cases: (1) every base table of schema commerce (information_schema.tables, table_type 'BASE TABLE') has an entry in TABLE_CLASSES, and every entry names a table that exists; (2) every 'with_parent' entry's parent exists, and unless the parent is 'stores' a foreign key from the table to the parent exists in pg_constraint; (3) every 'deleted' entry's kind is in RETENTION_KINDS and has a row in RETENTION_SEED, and the file named in `step` exists and its text contains `delete from commerce.<table>` (read with readFileSync); (4) the detector: a table that has a column named created_at, occurred_at, received_at, checked_at or day and whose class is 'reference' fails unless it is in a short KEPT list with a reason; (5) the scratch case: create table commerce.scratch_growing (id uuid primary key, created_at timestamptz not null default now()) inside the test, run the same check and expect it to name scratch_growing as a table with no class; then drop it.

Add a case 'every table that grows by time has a delete step': for every TABLE_CLASSES entry of class 'deleted', expect its kind to be in RETENTION_KINDS and, where enforcedBy of the seed row starts 'runRetention: ', expect the part after it to be a member of RETENTION_STEPS (import RETENTION_STEPS is server-only, so read src/server/retention.ts as text with the file's own `read()` helper and match the name inside the RETENTION_STEPS array).
